BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Status:** Draft analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team. Nothing below is cleared or approved. Any fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority, and none has been given.

## 0. Process points first

- **Every clause is open.** The Seller asks us to skip anything marked [STANDARD] because "both sides cleared" it. We have not cleared it. I have reviewed all clauses, including those marked [STANDARD].
- **"FINAL", "agreed at principal level" and "market standard" are assertions, not authority.** The Seller's market-context paragraph (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods) does not bind us. Our positions are set by the playbook.
- **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Bluefen consent, the Riverlark payoff, the bonus position, the DD-006 investigation and the Sandbar and Mossvale positions must all be refreshed before we rely on them.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start); 4.8m fallback only with Frost's written approval | Seller has opened at our fallback. Not authorised. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our number |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded (tipping) | 5x threshold and a deductible structure, which removes our first-dollar recovery |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Shortened without authority |
| Universal limitation | Any limitation applies to all Claims | Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override | Fundamental and specific claims pulled into general regime |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamentally inconsistent with playbook |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum enforceable extent, non-waivable | No fraud carve-out at all |
| Disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure | Direct conflict |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Direct conflict |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion | Consent-on-delivery and endeavours-only are both rejected |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Post-completion release, no undertaking |
| Bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) | Not itemised; "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude | Silently excluded |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Narrowed and labelled adequate |
| Export/privacy DD-006 (4.6, Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Materiality assertion; no preservation or investigation commitment |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Assertion not yet tested |
| Tax/IP (Seller's note) | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax/IP terms open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Treated as closed and folded into general regime |
| Title (DL 10) | Share register at DD-012 is evidence of title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof |

## 2. Reasoning and pushback by issue

**A. Liability architecture (caps, baskets, time limits).** The 20% cap is our fallback number, but the playbook does not allow it to be conceded without Frost's written authority identifying the draft. The Seller's thresholds are five times ours and deductible. Together with the 18-month period, that materially reduces recovery for the general warranty regime. Push back to 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar tipping basket and 24 months. Any move to the fallback requires written authority first.

**B. Fundamental/Title and universal limitations.** This is the most serious structural problem. Subjecting title and capacity to general caps, time limits and the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would strip protection from the claims we most need. Reject. Fundamental/Title should have a 100% cap, at least six years, and sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Separately, the draft has no fraud carve-out. Insert one covering fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, overriding caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum enforceable extent.

**C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** DL 1.1 and 1.2 deem the entire data room, accounts and public registers disclosed against all warranties. Combined with 8.3, which bars claims for anything discoverable, that would leave almost nothing for a warranty claim to attach to. Reject both. Require specific disclosure against each warranty. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. DL 1.4's denial that any consent is legally required should be resisted for Bluefen, Riverlark, the office lease and Mossvale. We need express confirmation of what is required.

**D. Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** This is a material customer consent and the disclosure confirms no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are both rejected. Require effective written consent and evidence that the conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion. If not satisfied, we need a right not to complete or a price-protection mechanism.

**E. Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m, as at September).** The debt is not repaid and no discharge is included. Under a debt-free, cash-free structure, the facility should be repaid at Completion from the price. Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. The Seller's post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Obtain a current figure because interest will have accrued since September.

**F. Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The disclosure confirms these are not in the funds flow and that payroll tax and superannuation treatment is unstated. The "matter for the Seller" response does not address the funds flow. Require the bonuses and triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded, and confirm which conditions (Completion and continued employment) are triggered and when.

**G. Ironquay IP (AUD 180,000 open).** DD-004 conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. The data room shows no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way, so we should neither accept nor dispute it as fact. Broaden the indemnity to cover title to the Project Materials and losses from non-transfer, not just the SOW3 payment. Preserve the SOW3 cure, which allows the Seller to clear the fees and obtain a confirmatory assignment.

**H. Export/privacy incident (DD-006; ~1,240 records).** The disclosure states the file went to an unintended external address and may contain names, business emails, roles and timestamps, but that it is not established whether anyone accessed it. "Not expected to be material" is an assertion. Require log preservation, a completed investigation with written updates, and disclosure of the scope and any access. We should not assume a breach, harm, notification duty or a number. Privacy counsel should confirm whether any notification assessment obligations under the Privacy Act are engaged. The Buyer should also consider a specific indemnity or covenant for privacy losses arising from the pre-Completion incident, without a quantified demand.

**I. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate).** The "ordinary-course" description is untested. The disclosure does not say whether the three renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Obtain the contracts and timing. Do not treat them as Debt or deduct them from price on current information. Assess them first.

**J. Office lease and Mossvale (DL 7 and 9).** Both disclosures are ambiguous about whether consent or notice is required because of the share sale. Obtain the lease and Mossvale provisions and confirm whether change of control is caught. This is a diligence gap, not a settled position.

**K. Tax and IP.** The Seller's statement that these are "settled under the general regime" is rejected. Tax and IP remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. They must not be folded into the general regime, and they should keep separate categories.

**L. Title.** DD-012 is an internal share register supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof. Require an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search for encumbrances, a certified register and evidence of the sale transfer, and board resolutions evidencing authority. The title warranty should be a fundamental warranty.

## 3. Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the efficiency note and "FINAL" framing.** Review all clauses. Do not accept market-standard, agreed or pre-cleared assertions.
2. **Reset the liability package** to 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months. Do not move to the fallback without Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Separate Fundamental/Title** with a 100% cap, six-year term, and outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Insert the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
5. **Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure** and delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence of conditions satisfied as a Completion condition. No endeavours-only or consent-on-delivery.
7. **Riverlark:** current payout, repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.
8. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow item or seller-funded.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the IP indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure; obtain the confirmatory assignment.
10. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require investigation updates, obtain privacy counsel's view, and consider a specific indemnity without a quantified demand.
11. **Sandbar:** obtain contracts and timing; no automatic Debt or price deduction.
12. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate.
13. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence.
14. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm whether consent or notice is required.
15. **Refresh all facts** as at today's date before the mark-up is sent.
